author: product-requirements-expert
title: A reader can narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory accept an optional specialty name and list only the veterinarians holding it. Matching is on the whole name, letter case disregarded. Naming nothing leaves today's behavior untouched.
acceptance_criteria: given a specialty that some veterinarians hold, when either form of the directory is requested for that specialty, then it lists those veterinarians and no others
given a specialty name differing from the stored name only by letter case, when either form is requested for it, then it matches
given only the opening letters of a specialty name, when either form is requested for them, then no veterinarian matches
given a specialty held by more veterinarians than fit one page, when the page form is requested for it, then the matches are listed a page at a time
given the page form narrowed to a specialty, when a later page is opened, then it stays narrowed to that specialty
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either form is requested for it, then the request succeeds and no veterinarian is listed
given a specialty that is empty or entirely spaces, when either form is requested for it, then the result matches a request naming no specialty at all
given no specialty named, when either form is requested, then it lists every veterinarian exactly as it did before specialties could be named
REQ-VET-003: given the clinic's veterinarians, when the machine-readable directory is requested, then it carries every veterinarian and each one's specialties in a single response
non_goals: free-text search over veterinarians, pets, or visits (NG-9 stands, narrowed only for whole-value narrowing of an already-published list)
narrowing by any attribute other than specialty
naming more than one specialty at once
a control on the page for choosing a specialty — the narrowing is addressable, not a form
filtering which of a matched veterinarian's specialties are displayed
notes: NUMBERING. Two fresh REQs, neither reusing the retired REQ-VET-002. REQ-VET-003 is the machine-readable directory as a supported surface; REQ-VET-004 is the narrowing. They are separate because the surface outlives the capability that motivated it — REQ-VET-003 must keep holding if the filter is ever dropped, and it constrains only one form while REQ-VET-004 constrains both. ONE requirement for the filter, not one per form: the matching rule is identical on both, and the forms differ only in representation, so splitting would duplicate every criterion. SLICING. One prd-entry covers both REQs. REQ-VET-003 alone is a single cycle pinning a document that already renders, which fails the too-small test and only makes sense beside its first consumer; its contract rides as the last acceptance criterion here. Combined, 7-9 TDD cycles, one deliverable surface (code). OWNER-FIXED EXTERNAL NAMES, for the design stage to record in system-design.md, deliberately kept out of the PRD to preserve its voice (it names no route anywhere): the parameter is named 'specialty' and the two surfaces are /vets.html and /vets. NON-GOAL ADR OWED. NG-9 is narrowed in docs/prd.md, but the project convention (docs/prd.md Non-Goals comment; docs/adr/README.md section Non-Goal ADRs) is that a non-goal change is recorded by an ADR named YYYY-MM-DD-non-goal-<slug>.md with an Implementation section reading 'Non-goal: NG-9'. None exists yet; this is the project's first human-made non-goal change. The PRD carries no ADR link until the file lands, and docs/adr/README.md needs its index row. Ownership is contested: this dispatch assigned authorship to the system-design-expert, but docs/adr/README.md and the product-requirements-expert write scope both assign non-goal ADRs to the product-requirements-expert. Resolve before dispatching the author. OPEN QUESTION RAISED. Whether a specialty named with surrounding spaces matches was not decided; recorded in Open Questions rather than invented. The all-spaces case is decided and covered above. PRD HOUSEKEEPING. The provenance banner now exempts requirements carrying a '(confirmed date)' mark, since REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004 are stated intent rather than derived behavior; the banner's open-question count was stale at ten and now reads four. REQ-VET-001 edge case 2, which called the second route an undocumented defect, is removed as answered.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Narrowing is a repository query, not a filter over a fetched collection. VetRepository gains two derived query methods mirroring its existing findAll pair — one paged for /vets.html, one unpaged Collection for /vets — resolving the specialty by whole name with letter case folded inside the query (Spring Data IgnoreCase, so the same request matches identically on H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL). VetController normalizes the optional parameter at the web boundary (strip; blank means absent) and chooses the narrowed or unnarrowed repository call; it holds no matching or paging rule of its own, so the architecture-principles Web controller row is not deviated from further. Paging is applied to the narrowed result by the repository, which is what makes the page count and the later-page criterion come out right. The genuinely new ground is the interaction with the vets cache: the narrowed query is deliberately NOT @Cacheable, recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-05-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-query.md and as current state in docs/system-design.md section Persistence. Routes and the parameter name are recorded in the new docs/system-design.md section Published web surface. REQ-VET-003 needs no code beyond keeping /vets serving the whole collection in one response; it retires the Known Defects row that called that route pending removal.
integration_points: VetRepository gains a narrowed read over the Vet.specialties association (@ManyToMany to Specialty, name inherited from NamedEntity); Spring Data resolves the property path from the method name, so no @Query is needed

VetController.showVetList gains the optional parameter and passes the normalized value to the narrowed or unnarrowed paged call; VetController.showResourcesVetList does the same against the unpaged pair. One private normalization helper serves both handlers so the strip / blank-means-absent rule is written once
vetList.html pagination links must carry the specialty forward; the model gains the normalized value for the template to read
CacheConfiguration is untouched: the vets cache keeps its two cached reads and gains no third

patterns.description: findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable) — the standing precedent for narrowing at the repository with paging applied to the narrowed result; likewise uncached. Use = semantics here (whole name), not StartingWith, since prefix matching is explicitly excluded
strip() the caller's value and treat the empty result as the broadest query — the existing web-boundary normalization this slice mirrors for the specialty parameter
findPaginated / addPaginationModel — the existing paging shape the narrowed path extends rather than replaces

risks.risk: VetControllerTests stubs VetRepository with @MockitoBean, so the case-insensitivity, whole-name, and no-prefix criteria would pass vacuously there — the stub returns whatever it is told regardless of the argument
risks.mitigation: Verify matching semantics in ClinicServiceTests (@DataJpaTest against real H2 with the seeded specialties radiology, surgery, dentistry). The controller tests verify parameter pass-through, paging, and the blank/absent equivalence; the repository tests verify the match rule

risks.risk: Carrying the specialty through the pagination links by string concatenation into the href (the template's existing __${...}__ preprocessing style) would emit unencoded caller-supplied text into a URL attribute — a parameter-injection and XSS vector that Thymeleaf's default HTML escaping does not cover for this construct
risks.mitigation: Use the parameterized link expression @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes each parameter and omits a null one. The blank-means-absent rule makes an empty rendering harmless either way

risks.risk: Filtering after the page is cut would page the whole directory and then show only part of a page, breaking the paging and later-page criteria
risks.mitigation: The narrowing is the repository query; Pageable is applied by that same query

risks.risk: Adding @Cacheable to the narrowed query would make an unbounded caller-supplied string the key of a cache with no size limit, no eviction, and no expiry
risks.mitigation: The narrowed methods carry no @Cacheable; the decision and the rejected alternative are in docs/adr/2026-08-05-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-query.md so a later reader does not 'fix' the inconsistency

risks.risk: A paged derived query traversing a to-many association can return duplicate rows or force Hibernate to page in memory
risks.mitigation: Neither applies: the derived query joins for the predicate rather than fetch-joining, so paging stays in SQL, and a Vet holds a given Specialty at most once (Set-valued association), so at most one joined row per Vet matches

notes: DURABLE MEMORY WRITTEN. (1) New ADR docs/adr/2026-08-05-uncached-specialty-narrowed-vet-query.md. author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Reflected-value handling: the caller-supplied specialty reaches the rendered page only through parameterized link expressions (vetList.html:38,44,50,56,62). Every one of the five page links uses the @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})} form; no __${...}__ preprocessing survives in vetList.html, and the value is never rendered into body text or any other attribute. Thymeleaf URL-encodes the link parameter and HTML-escapes the attribute; VetControllerTests pins radiology"&evil=1 rendering as radiology%22%26evil%3D1 with neither radiology" nor evil=1 present. Swept the whole templates/ tree for th:utext, th:inline and [( )] unescaped inlining - none exist anywhere, so the reflected-value class has no second instance.

Cache poisoning by unbounded growth is genuinely avoided: grep over src/main confirms @Cacheable appears only on the two pre-existing findAll methods (VetRepository:45,55); both new findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase overloads (VetRepository:72,86) carry only @Transactional(readOnly = true). CacheConfiguration is untouched, and no other code path lets a caller-supplied string reach a cache key - the vets cache key derives solely from the no-arg/Pageable findAll signatures. The Javadoc on both methods states the constraint at the point where a future edit would break it, and the ADR records it.

Query construction is injection-safe: both new reads are Spring Data derived methods over Vet.specialties.name with IgnoreCase, which JPA renders as a bound parameter under upper(). No @Query, EntityManager, createQuery, or string-concatenated JPQL/SQL is introduced; grep over src/main/java confirms the only @Query in the codebase is the pre-existing parameterless PetTypeRepository ordering query. The existing Threat Model 'SQL injection' row's stated mitigation continues to hold.

Web-boundary normalization (VetController.normalizeSpecialty) is total and side-effect-free: null stays null, strip-then-empty collapses to null, and the single helper feeds both surfaces, so the HTML and JSON handlers cannot diverge in what they treat as 'absent'. No length cap is needed for security here - an oversize value is a bound query parameter that matches nothing and is never cached.

The JSON surface exposes nothing the HTML page does not. /vets?specialty=... returns the same Vet/Vets projection as before over a narrowed row set; the caller's string is not echoed into the document, and Vets/Vet serialization is unchanged. Reinstating the full collection when the parameter is absent restores prior behavior rather than widening it.

Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle, settings.gradle, gradle.properties and gradle/ carry zero delta in the change set, so no new dependency or version enters the tree and the pass introduces no new CVE surface.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the veterinarian directory by specialty

blast_radius.note: Production reach is one package plus its template: VetRepository gains two derived reads, VetController gains one boundary helper and a null check on each of its two handlers, vetList.html rewrites its five page links. No sensitive paths, no build or config or schema files, no dependency delta, and no other caller of either route (only the layout menu item, which passes no parameter). The 44 hunks and 3 modules are docs and tests, not spread in the code.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every prod hunk for behavior that outruns the description and found none. The unnarrowed paths are the old ones unchanged (findAll and findAll(Pageable), PageRequest.of(page - 1, 5) untouched); normalizeSpecialty is total (null stays null, strip-then-empty collapses to null) and feeds both surfaces from one place, so HTML and JSON cannot diverge on what counts as absent. The riskiest hunk is the pagination-link rewrite, which touches the unnarrowed page every visitor sees: the old inline preprocessing becomes a parameterized link expression, and a test pins that the rendered link is still /vets.html?page=2 with no specialty= anywhere. The uncached narrowed query is a deliberate ADR-backed asymmetry with its siblings, stated in Javadoc at the point a future edit would break it.

test_adequacy.note: The tests would fail against a broken implementation, and they are placed where they can. The match rule itself (whole name, case folded, prefix does not match, paging cut from the narrowed set) is pinned in ClinicServiceTests against real H2 and the real seeded rows, not in the stubbed controller test where any argument would pass. The controller tests assert the web boundary's own share: which repository read is chosen (verify plus never on the alternate), the exact stripped value and Pageable that reach it, and a hostile specialty value rendering into the page links encoded, with neither the raw quote nor the injected parameter present. One PRD edge case rides on construction rather than a test: that a matched vet still shows all its specialties, which no code path trims.

reviewer_hedging.note: Full four-reviewer battery on a high-risk full-diff plan, all four approved with empty findings lists after the single round-1 naming autofix was fixed and re-approved. Nothing reads as approval-with-reservation: the one deliberate omission, leaving the system-design Security Context and Threat Model un-updated for the new input surface, was put to the security- and doc-reviewers explicitly and each reasoned it to not-a-finding against the existing injection and XSS rows rather than waving it through. It stays a real post-merge doc-sync item.

scope_deviation.note: The lone structural trigger, design_revisions = 1, resolves on reading to bookkeeping: the superseding design-block only added docs/adr/README.md to a path list so the autofix audit would cover it, and the abort it settled changed no code. Zero build retries, zero consultations. The code diff sits inside the prd-entry file targets; ClinicServiceTests is the one extra file, added because the design-block split the match rule down to the repository tier. The docs delta is the widest part of the change, and every piece of it traces to a stated product decision rather than to implementation drift.

rationale: Contained, well-pinned code with a full clean battery behind it; the pagination rewrite is the only hunk touching existing behavior and a test holds it.
